title: Requests, permission and rules: do, may, must not, must

relationships.label: Recognize a strong prohibition versus a polite negative request

exercises.translation: Please write your name here. Use 書く (かく) with the てください request pattern; fill the whole verb phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: 書く gives 書いて, then ください requests writing.

options.label: 書いてください
options.rationale: 書く gives 書いて, then ください requests writing.

options.label: 書かないでください
options.rationale: This expresses a negative request, not the requested message.

options.label: 書いてはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses prohibition, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: Please read this letter. Use 読む (よむ) with てください; fill the whole verb phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: 読む gives the voiced て-form 読んで; the request is 読んでください.

options.label: 読んでください
options.rationale: 読む gives the voiced て-form 読んで; the request is 読んでください.

options.label: 読まないでください
options.rationale: This expresses a negative request, not the requested message.

options.label: 読んではいけません
options.rationale: This expresses prohibition, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: Please do not write your name here. Use 書く (かく) with ないでください; fill the whole verb phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: Use the negative 書かない plus でください, not 書かなくてください.

options.label: 書かないでください
options.rationale: Use the negative 書かない plus でください, not 書かなくてください.

options.label: 書いてください
options.rationale: This expresses a positive request, not the requested message.

options.label: 書いてもいいです
options.rationale: This expresses permission, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: Please do not open the window. Use 開ける (あける) with ないでください; fill the whole verb phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: Remove ichidan る, make 開けない, then add でください.

options.label: 開けないでください
options.rationale: Remove ichidan る, make 開けない, then add でください.

options.label: 開けてください
options.rationale: This expresses a positive request, not the requested message.

options.label: 開けてもいいです
options.rationale: This expresses permission, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: You may sit in this chair. Express permission using 座る (すわる) and てもいいです; fill the whole verb phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: 座ってもいいです permits sitting; it neither prohibits nor requires it.

options.label: 座ってもいいです
options.rationale: 座ってもいいです permits sitting; it neither prohibits nor requires it.

options.label: 座ってはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses prohibition, not the requested message.

options.label: 座らなくてはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses obligation, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: You may take photos here. Use 撮る (とる) and てもいいです to express permission; fill the whole verb phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: 撮る is godan; 撮ってもいいです grants permission.

options.label: 撮ってもいいです
options.rationale: 撮る is godan; 撮ってもいいです grants permission.

options.label: 撮ってはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses prohibition, not the requested message.

options.label: 撮らなくてはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses obligation, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: You must not enter this room. Use 入る (はいる) and an ordinary polite ては prohibition ending (いけません or なりません); fill the complete phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: 入っては + a negative prohibition ending rules out entering. なりません is also accepted; it often sounds more formal.
acceptedAnswers: はいってはいけません
はいってはなりません

options.label: 入ってはいけません
options.rationale: 入っては + a negative prohibition ending rules out entering. なりません is also accepted; it often sounds more formal.

options.label: 入ってもいいです
options.rationale: This expresses permission, not the requested message.

options.label: 入らなくてはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses obligation, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: You must not drink this water. Use 飲む (のむ) and an ordinary polite ては prohibition ending (いけません or なりません); fill the complete phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: The voiced て-form is 飲んで, so the prohibition begins 飲んでは.

options.label: 飲んではいけません
options.rationale: The voiced て-form is 飲んで, so the prohibition begins 飲んでは.

options.label: 飲んでもいいです
options.rationale: This expresses permission, not the requested message.

options.label: 飲まなくてはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses obligation, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: You must write your name here. Use 書く (かく) and the polite なくては obligation family (いけません or なりません); fill the complete phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: 書かない becomes 書かなくては; forbidding not writing produces the obligation to write.
acceptedAnswers: 書かなくてはいけません
かかなくてはいけません
書かなくてはなりません
かかなくてはなりません

options.label: 書かなくてはいけません
options.rationale: 書かない becomes 書かなくては; forbidding not writing produces the obligation to write.

options.label: 書いてはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses prohibition, not the requested message.

options.label: 書いてもいいです
options.rationale: This expresses permission, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: I must return home today. Use 帰る (かえる) and the polite なくては obligation family (いけません or なりません); fill the complete phrase.
exercises.evidence: The question specifies the intended message and the ending family to practise.
exercises.explanation: Godan 帰る gives 帰らない, then 帰らなくては + the ending. This is must return, not must not return.
acceptedAnswers: 帰らなくてはいけません
かえらなくてはいけません
帰らなくてはなりません
かえらなくてはなりません

options.label: 帰らなくてはいけません
options.rationale: Godan 帰る gives 帰らない, then 帰らなくては + the ending. This is must return, not must not return.

options.label: 帰ってはいけません
options.rationale: This expresses prohibition, not the requested message.

options.label: 帰ってもいいです
options.rationale: This expresses permission, not the requested message.

exercises.translation: It is fine if the hotel is inexpensive. Formation: use 安い (やすい, inexpensive) with the plain acceptability pattern ending in てもいい／でもいい. Fill the whole predicate; no final です.
exercises.evidence: Select the attachment for this predicate type, keeping the requested plain ending.
exercises.explanation: An い-adjective changes い to く before てもいい.

options.label: 安くてもいい
options.rationale: An い-adjective changes い to く before てもいい.

options.label: 安いでもいい
options.rationale: This applies the other predicate type's attachment to the supplied word.

exercises.translation: It is fine if the box is big. Formation: use 大きい (おおきい, big) with the plain acceptability pattern ending in てもいい／でもいい. Fill the whole predicate; no final です.
exercises.evidence: Select the attachment for this predicate type, keeping the requested plain ending.
exercises.explanation: Use the くて form of 大きい followed by もいい.

options.label: 大きくてもいい
options.rationale: Use the くて form of 大きい followed by もいい.

options.label: 大きいでもいい
options.rationale: This applies the other predicate type's attachment to the supplied word.

exercises.translation: It is fine if the room is quiet. Formation: use 静か (しずか, quiet) with the plain acceptability pattern ending in てもいい／でもいい. Fill the whole predicate; no final です.
exercises.evidence: Select the attachment for this predicate type, keeping the requested plain ending.
exercises.explanation: A な-adjective takes でもいい after its stem; it does not acquire くて.

options.label: 静かでもいい
options.rationale: A な-adjective takes でもいい after its stem; it does not acquire くて.

options.label: 静かくてもいい
options.rationale: This applies the other predicate type's attachment to the supplied word.

exercises.translation: A pencil is acceptable too. Formation: use 鉛筆 (えんぴつ, pencil) with the plain acceptability pattern ending in てもいい／でもいい. Fill the whole predicate; no final です.
exercises.evidence: Select the attachment for this predicate type, keeping the requested plain ending.
exercises.explanation: The noun takes でもいい. This accepts a pencil as an option; it does not require a pencil.

options.label: 鉛筆でもいい
options.rationale: The noun takes でもいい. This accepts a pencil as an option; it does not require a pencil.

options.label: 鉛筆くてもいい
options.rationale: This applies the other predicate type's attachment to the supplied word.

exercises.translation: You must not eat here. Interpret the complete utterance: 禁止 (きんし, must not do) or 義務 (ぎむ, must do).
exercises.evidence: 食べちゃ contracts 食べては; this prohibits eating.
exercises.explanation: 食べちゃ contracts 食べては; this prohibits eating. Read both negative layers where present.

options.label: 禁止
options.rationale: 食べちゃ contracts 食べては; this prohibits eating.

options.label: 義務
options.rationale: This reverses the message in this utterance.

exercises.translation: You must not drink this water. Interpret the complete utterance: 禁止 (きんし, must not do) or 義務 (ぎむ, must do).
exercises.evidence: 飲んじゃ contracts 飲んでは; this prohibits drinking.
exercises.explanation: 飲んじゃ contracts 飲んでは; this prohibits drinking. Read both negative layers where present.

options.label: 禁止
options.rationale: 飲んじゃ contracts 飲んでは; this prohibits drinking.

options.label: 義務
options.rationale: This reverses the message in this utterance.

exercises.translation: I have to do my homework (an ordinary standalone obligation in this scene). Interpret the complete utterance: 禁止 (きんし, must not do) or 義務 (ぎむ, must do).
exercises.evidence: しなくちゃ is short for しなくては, with an obligation ending understood here.
exercises.explanation: しなくちゃ is short for しなくては, with an obligation ending understood here. Read both negative layers where present.

options.label: 禁止
options.rationale: This reverses the message in this utterance.

options.label: 義務
options.rationale: しなくちゃ is short for しなくては, with an obligation ending understood here.

exercises.translation: I have to go now (an ordinary standalone obligation in this scene). Interpret the complete utterance: 禁止 (きんし, must not do) or 義務 (ぎむ, must do).
exercises.evidence: 行かなきゃ comes from 行かなければ; the understood obligation means must go.
exercises.explanation: 行かなきゃ comes from 行かなければ; the understood obligation means must go. Read both negative layers where present.

options.label: 禁止
options.rationale: This reverses the message in this utterance.

options.label: 義務
options.rationale: 行かなきゃ comes from 行かなければ; the understood obligation means must go.

exercises.translation: A forceful warning says: Do not enter. Identify the form used: 強い禁止 (つよいきんし, strong prohibition) or 丁寧な依頼 (ていねいないらい, polite request). This is recognition, not advice to use the forceful form.
exercises.evidence: Dictionary 入る plus final な is the strong prohibition, not a general polite request.
exercises.explanation: Dictionary 入る plus final な is the strong prohibition, not a general polite request. A polite form can still be direct or authoritative; context determines appropriateness.

options.label: 強い禁止
options.rationale: Dictionary 入る plus final な is the strong prohibition, not a general polite request.

options.label: 丁寧な依頼
options.rationale: That is not the grammatical form quoted here.

exercises.evidence: Dictionary 触る plus な is strongly prohibitive in this quoted warning.
exercises.explanation: Dictionary 触る plus な is strongly prohibitive in this quoted warning. A polite form can still be direct or authoritative; context determines appropriateness.
